units.translation: Eustathius p. 600, 43: σχίσματα γάρ τινα καὶ θύσανοι [for there are certain clefts and tassels], whence ἀρειθύσανοι [Ares-tassels] according to Pausanias, "Αρεος θύσανοι [tassels of Ares], as it were ἀποσχίσματα [offshoots], in Aeschylus' Prometheus Unbound (fr. 200). Hesychius: ἀρθύσανοι [Ares-tassels]: ἀποσχίσματα καὶ ἀποβλαστήματα [offshoots and sprouts]. ἀριθύσανοι [charioteers]: ἡνίοχοι [charioteers]. In the former gloss the order of letters requires ἀρθρύσανοι (as Favorinus wrote), in the latter ἀρειθύσανοι. Lobeck contends against Eustathius that the word is ἀρειμανεῖς [raging with Ares] or Ἄρει κατόχους [possessed by Ares]. Pathol. Elem. vol. 1 p. 341.

In the former gloss the order of letters requires ἀρθρύσανοι [Ares-tassels] (as Favorinus wrote), in the latter ἀρειθύσανοι [Ares-tassels]. Lobeck contends against Eustathius that the word is ἀρειμανεῖς [raging with Ares] or Ἄρει κατόχους [possessed by Ares]. Pathol. Elem. vol. 1 p. 341.

In Homer ἀρηίφατοι [slain in war] are those who are killed in battle: hence ἀρείφατοι φόνοι [slain in war murders] in Euripides Suppl. 603. In a broader sense it is used for ἄρειος [warlike], i.e. Martial.
where ἀρείφατος [slain in war] is explained as ἐν πολέμοις φονευόμενος [being killed in wars], the Florentine codex in Miller, Mélanges p. 41 adds

the words which are added, καὶ καρτερικὸς καὶ πολεμικὸς ἀρείφατος [both strong and warlike, slain in war], are nothing other than explanations of the word ἀρείφατος [slain in war], just as in the preceding Etym. the words ἀρειμάνιος [raging with Ares] and ἀρείφατος [slain in war] are explained by πολεμικός [warlike]. See Thes. vol. 1, 2 p. 1930.
